From 30945d31e5761436d9eba6b8cff468a5f7c9c266 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Nuno=20S=C3=A1?= <nuno.sa@analog.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Sep 2019 14:49:43 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] hwmon: Fix HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM mask
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Both HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM and HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM were using
BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm).

Fixes: aa7f29b07c870 ("hwmon: Add support for power min, lcrit, min_alarm and lcrit_alarm")
CC: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Nuno Sá <nuno.sa@analog.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20190924124945.491326-2-nuno.sa@analog.com
Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net>

diff --git a/include/linux/hwmon.h b/include/linux/hwmon.h
index 04c36b7a61dd..72579168189d 100644
--- a/include/linux/hwmon.h
+++ b/include/linux/hwmon.h
@@ -235,7 +235,7 @@ enum hwmon_power_attributes {
 #define HWMON_P_LABEL			BIT(hwmon_power_label)
 #define HWMON_P_ALARM			BIT(hwmon_power_alarm)
 #define HWMON_P_CAP_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_cap_alarm)
-#define HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)
+#define HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_min_alarm)
 #define HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)
 #define HWMON_P_LCRIT_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_lcrit_alarm)
 #define HWMON_P_CRIT_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_crit_alarm)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `include/linux/hwmon.h`**
   - The definition of `HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM` was changed from:
     ```c
     #define HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)
     ```
     to:
     ```c
     #define HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_min_alarm)
     ```
   - The definition of `HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM` remains unchanged.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `include/linux/hwmon.h` corrects the definition of `HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM` to use the appropriate mask for `hwmon_power_min_alarm` instead of incorrectly using the mask for `hwmon_power_max_alarm`. This change ensures that the minimum alarm functionality works correctly, addressing a bug introduced in a previous commit (identified by the hash `aa7f29b07c870`). The relationship is that the fix directly addresses the incorrect behavior caused by the previous definition, thereby improving the accuracy of the hardware monitoring functionality.

hwmon: Fix HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM mask
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Both HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM and HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM were using
BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm).

Fixes: aa7f29b07c870 ("hwmon: Add support for power min, lcrit, min_alarm and lcrit_alarm")
CC: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Nuno Sá <nuno.sa@analog.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20190924124945.491326-2-nuno.sa@analog.com
Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by both `HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM` and `HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM` incorrectly using the same mask (`BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)`), which led to improper handling of minimum alarm conditions in the hardware monitoring system. This misconfiguration meant that the minimum alarm functionality did not operate as intended, potentially causing incorrect alarm triggers or failures to trigger alarms when necessary.

 #define HWMON_P_CAP_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_cap_alarm)
-#define HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)
+#define HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_min_alarm)
 #define HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)
 #define HWMON_P_LCRIT_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_lcrit_alarm)

Reason:
Both `HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM` and `HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM` were incorrectly defined to use the same mask (`BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)`), which caused the minimum alarm functionality to be misconfigured. This resulted in improper handling of minimum alarm conditions, leading to potential incorrect alarm triggers or failures to trigger alarms when necessary.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_min_alarm)
#define HWMON_P_MAX_ALARM		BIT(hwmon_power_max_alarm)
```
Reason:
The patch corrects the definition of `HWMON_P_MIN_ALARM` to use the appropriate mask (`BIT(hwmon_power_min_alarm)`), ensuring that the minimum alarm functionality operates as intended and does not interfere with the maximum alarm functionality. This fix allows for proper handling of minimum alarm conditions in the hardware monitoring system.
